Merge over-split clone leaves with a permutation-calibrated split test

Source: R/clones_discovery.R
merge_clones.Rd

Bottom-up: each round, every clone's n_nb nearest clones (Ward distance between the clones' centroids in the smoothed PC space) are candidate pairs; the pairs are tested in order of distance with the clone contrast (split_test) against the q-quantile of the same statistic on random splits of the pooled pair at matching sizes (n_perm permutations, sequential early stop), and non-different pairs are merged (each clone at most once per round). Stops when every candidate pair of the remaining clones differs at the budget (q = 0.999 = 1 false split per 1,000 tests). Each half is subsampled to max_cells cells (observed and null alike). Nearest neighbours rather than Ward siblings only: once two sibling clones differ, a sibling-only rule never compares either of them with any other clone.

Usage

merge_clones(
  feat_long,
  votes,
  atoms,
  regions,
  leaves,
  tree,
  q = 0.999,
  n_perm = 200,
  seed = 1,
  rho = 0.01,
  classes = c("arm", "20Mb"),
  cells = NULL,
  max_cells = 250,
  cdata = NULL,
  depth_delta = 0.2,
  n_nb = 3
)

Arguments

feat_long

features long table

votes, atoms, regions

votes, atoms, regions

leaves

named leaf labels (names = cells), from discover_clones()

tree

the discover_clones() result (its smooth coordinates are used) or a cells x dims matrix

q

null quantile (budget)

n_perm

permutations per test

seed

RNG seed

rho

beta-binomial overdispersion

classes

region classes of the contrast

cells

cell names in vote index order

max_cells

subsample per half

cdata

optional pre-computed contrast_data()

depth_delta

minimal depth effect (log2) of the contrast

n_nb

nearest clones tested per clone and round

Value

list(clones = named integer labels, tests = data.table of all tests)
